title: plugin-auth: a sign-in by a SCIM-deactivated user is refused as a generic BANNED_USER ("You have been banned…"); refuse it with a distinct, machine-readable deactivation cause
body:
triage#1 · os-zhuang · session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U

Split from #32087 on `domain:ui#2`'s routing request (mailbox 6797013916). The platform half goes first (「平台相关的功能，应该尽量先改平台」).

## Measured

From the SCIM run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3667 (comment 6783961273 on #32087, pin `e24136c2`): an employee deactivated through SCIM (`active:false`) who then tries the password sign-in is refused with the vendor's `BANNED_USER` and the text "You have been banned from this application. Please contact support if you believe this is an error."

The ban carries the reason `Deactivated via SCIM`, but nothing in the refusal tells a client that this is an organization deactivation rather than a disciplinary ban. On `origin/main` `7d82b2da`, no platform code maps `BANNED_USER` or the ban reason; the text is better-auth's.

## Do

1. Read where `plugin-auth`'s SCIM `active:false` path sets the ban, and what the sign-in refusal returns: code, message and any details.
2. Make the refusal for a SCIM-deactivated user carry a distinct, documented cause that a client can branch on. Either a code of its own, or `BANNED_USER` with a stable `details.cause`. No end-user copy belongs on the server.
3. Keep ordinary bans unchanged. ⛔ The refusal names no IdP internals or other user's data.
4. Pin both: a SCIM-deactivated sign-in and an admin ban.

The ui half, which maps the new cause to "Your account has been deactivated by your organization. Contact your administrator.", is its own `domain:ui` card, blocked by this one.

Lane: `domain:server` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth`). p2: end-user wording. The account is refused correctly; only the message misleads.
